title: Unified Runtime Logging And MCP Debugging Roadmap
goal: Unify Odysseus runtime logs, ledgers and Telegram diagnostics behind one redacted event model and expose full read-only MCP debugging and analysis capabilities for operators and coding agents.
why: Odysseus currently has several useful logs and ledgers, but they are fragmented across app logs, AI activity, agent runs, Telegram, scheduler, Universal Inbox, memory, RaptorGraph and background jobs.
Troubleshooting recurring issues such as missing Telegram replies, failed OCR/STT, scheduler reminders, Nextcloud import, memory writes and RaptorGraph maintenance needs a shared correlation model.
The Debian observability stack should collect already-redacted structured events instead of scraping an inconsistent mix of prose logs.
MCP should become the safe debugging workbench: broad analysis and diagnosis, but read-only by default and gated for any live mutation.

related_roadmaps.relationship: Downstream observability stack consumes the unified events and MCP diagnostics defined here.

security_and_ops: CrowdSec alerts and decisions once enabled

label_cardinality_rules: Prometheus/Loki labels may use surface, component, event_type, status and severity.
Do not use raw IDs, filenames, document titles, prompts, URLs with query strings or user text as labels.
Correlation IDs belong in event payloads and query parameters, not high-cardinality metric labels.

mcp_debugging_target.principle: Full debugging and analysis surface, read-only by default.
mcp_debugging_target.server_scope: Local Odysseus MCP server or dedicated debug MCP server, token-authenticated and not exposed remotely without a separate gate.
mcp_debugging_target.write_or_remediation_policy: Any mutation such as task retry, scheduler pause, CrowdSec remediation, service restart, log deletion or replay requires an explicit gated tool and operator confirmation.

parallelization_model.rule: Multiagent execution must assign disjoint write scopes. Telegram, LLM core, MCP server registration and RaptorGraph files are hot paths and should be edited serially unless a coordinator explicitly partitions exact files.

safe_parallel_tracks.reason: Schema and observability label policy are docs/model work and can proceed before adapters.
Runtime adapters and MCP contract can be developed against the same envelope with separate files.
Raptor provenance and redacted bundle generation are separable if they only meet at the event query API.

avoid_parallel_tracks.reason: Telegram plugin is already a hotspot.
MCP registration and tool policy must remain coherent.
Do not start shipping logs before the inventory and redaction policy are known.

slice_queue.goal: Inventory every existing log, ledger and diagnostic surface and classify it by privacy risk, owner scope, retention and correlation fields.
slice_queue.done_when: A machine-readable inventory lists all current log sources, what they contain, what is safe for Loki, and which fields need redaction or hashing.
slice_queue.evidence: Created docs/plans/unified-runtime-logging-inventory.json with source groups for app logs, AI activity, agent runs, agent tasks, memory provenance, Telegram, Universal Inbox, scheduler/calendar, diagnostics routes, mount audit, background jobs and Podman/systemd ops. The inventory classifies privacy risk, Loki suitability, correlation fields and forbidden raw fields.

slice_queue.goal: Implement the shared runtime event envelope and redaction rules as a small backend module.
slice_queue.done_when: All event writers can create redacted events with correlation_id, surface, component, event_type, status, severity and privacy metadata.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/runtime_event_envelope.py with required runtime event fields, owner hash/scope handling, privacy levels, safe statuses/severities, forbidden field and marker rejection, host-path hashing for references, metadata validation and a low-cardinality Loki projection. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 7 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Emit unified events for the complete Telegram flow from inbound update to reply, including STT, OCR, Inbox, Agent turn and control commands.
slice_queue.done_when: A Telegram message can be traced by correlation_id through receive, allow/block, parse, media pipeline, agent/control handling and reply status.
notes: Do not store raw chat IDs as event fields.
Use stable hashed chat/message references for correlation.
This slice must not run in parallel with other Telegram plugin edits.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented Telegram runtime_event envelopes and stable correlation_id fields in plugins/telegram/stores.py for inbound messages, system/control events and outbound reply delivery. Existing polling paths for control commands, Universal Inbox attachments/exports, voice retries, session bridge, agent turns and replies all persist through the store event layer, so they are traceable by redacted correlation metadata without raw chat IDs or raw message text in the runtime_event. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 91 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Add unified event emission to scheduler, Universal Inbox, Nextcloud transfer and memory write-intent flows.
slice_queue.done_when: Reminder failures, inbox extraction failures, Nextcloud copy/write blockers and memory write outcomes are diagnosable by correlation_id.
tests: venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_task_scheduler_delivery.py tests/test_universal_inbox_pipeline.py tests/test_universal_inbox_memory_write_intent.py tests/test_nextcloud_source_provider.py tests/test_runtime_event_envelope.py -q
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented redacted runtime_event and correlation_id fields for scheduler delivery decisions, Universal Inbox pipeline reports, Universal Inbox memory write intents and Nextcloud source readiness reports. Events expose status, component, safe counts and policy outcomes without raw task text, document content, chat IDs, host paths, WebDAV endpoints or secrets. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 34 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Connect RaptorGraph maintenance, provenance and memory write logs to the shared event envelope.
slice_queue.done_when: RaptorGraph rebuild/readiness/maintenance and memory writes produce redacted events that can be traced back to source docs/tasks without exposing private content.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented redacted runtime_event and correlation_id fields for RaptorGraph candidate mappings and MemoryService remember/recall/delete operations. Existing memory provenance ledger tests confirm memory, RaptorGraph and user interaction provenance remains redacted; new tests verify runtime events do not expose raw memory text or raw queries. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 18 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Define and implement the read-only MCP diagnostic tool contract for unified logs, metrics, Telegram, scheduler, inbox, memory, RaptorGraph, models and ops summaries.
slice_queue.done_when: MCP exposes broad read-only debugging tools and blocks all mutation/remediation by default.
required_tool_properties: operator confirmation required for any future write/remediation tool
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented mcp_servers/debug_server.py with a read-only, bounded and redacted diagnostic contract covering event traces, Telegram, scheduler, inbox, Nextcloud, memory, RaptorGraph, model/agent, Podman and debug bundle summary tools. Added the debug server to built-in MCP registration and allowed only the explicit debug_readonly tool category in src/mcp_server_tool_policy.py; unknown or remediation-like tools remain blocked. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 11 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Build a redacted debug bundle generator that collects correlated events, summaries and counters for one incident.
slice_queue.done_when: A missing Telegram reply, failed reminder or blocked memory write can produce a compact redacted bundle for review or GitHub issue attachment.

slice_queue.goal: Define the Loki/Grafana/Prometheus label contract so live log shipping remains queryable and low-cardinality.
slice_queue.done_when: Dashboard labels and log fields are documented with explicit forbidden labels and retention assumptions.
slice_queue.evidence: Created docs/plans/unified-runtime-logging-dashboard-label-contract.json with allowed Loki and Prometheus labels, forbidden high-cardinality/private labels, allowed and forbidden event payload fields, metric families, dashboard sections, retention defaults and acceptance checks.

slice_queue.goal: Add optional read-only clients for Prometheus and Loki queries behind MCP diagnostics, disabled unless configured.
slice_queue.done_when: Configured deployments can query Prometheus/Loki through bounded read-only tools; unconfigured deployments return readiness blockers.
notes: No live network query in unit tests.
Use fake clients and explicit config gates.

slice_queue.goal: Run one bounded live smoke on the Debian server after the event schema, MCP tools and log shipping are configured.
slice_queue.done_when: A harmless Telegram diagnostic flow is visible through unified events, MCP debug query, Loki/Grafana and Prometheus counters.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Approve one harmless live Telegram/debug flow on Debian after repo-only slices pass.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: Live Telegram, Loki or Prometheus queries could reveal operational metadata or notify the wrong target.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Decide whether the debug MCP server remains local-only or is reachable through a protected channel.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: A broad debugging surface can leak sensitive operational metadata if exposed.

blocks: Any MCP tool that restarts services, retries jobs, mutates scheduler state, deletes logs or changes CrowdSec decisions
gate_queue.decision_needed: Approve specific remediation tools one by one after read-only diagnostics are proven.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: Debugging could accidentally become unsafe remote control.

definition_of_done: All major Odysseus runtime subsystems emit or can be mapped into one redacted event envelope.
Telegram message failures are traceable end-to-end without raw chat IDs or private content.
Scheduler, Inbox, Nextcloud, Memory and RaptorGraph failures are diagnosable by correlation_id.
A read-only MCP debug server exposes comprehensive analysis tools with bounded redacted output.
Optional Loki/Prometheus adapters support Grafana-era observability without making the app depend on live observability services.
A redacted debug bundle can be generated for one incident.

recommended_next_action.reason: ULOG-0 through ULOG-5 plus ULOG-7 are complete; the next ULOG repo-only slice is the redacted debug bundle generator.
